sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Grocery Store Retailing of Imported Asian Condiments and Veg

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codified tradition, EU primary-law supremacy, commercial law codified in the 1915 Company Law and the specialized Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp)

Luxembourg-PRC Bilateral Investment Treaty signed 31 March 1994, entered into force 6 June 1997

Luxembourg-Thailand Double Taxation Agreement in force since 1996

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (consolidated by amendments of 27 October 2010, 18 December 2015, 13 February 2018, and 17 May 2020); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 (SCSp regime); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 6 March 2023 restricting public access pursuant to CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and annual accounts; Grand-Ducal regulations implementing RBE filing mechanics.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE accessible to the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit, supervisory authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities, and persons demonstrating legitimate interest; no general public search)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de societe) executed before a Luxembourg notary or as a written private deed (sous seing prive) with certified signatures and date certainty
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public or certified Luxembourg legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial certification; Hague Apostille not required for Luxembourg-origin deeds

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-conviction (extrait du casier judiciaire) or equivalent good-conduct certificate for each general partner (associe commandite) and each manager (gerant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or criminal records registry of each partner's country of habitual residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for contracting states (PRC accession effective 7 November 2023) or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true passport copy, proof of residential address, and source-of-funds declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent consular authority, notary, or registered AML/CFT professional in the document-origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization contingent on the issuer state's convention status

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Food business operator registration dossier and establishment approval conditions under EU Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004
Commercial establishment permit application (autorisation d'etablissement) filed through the guichet.lu one-stop-shop
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of the Economy, Direction Generale des Classes moyennes, and the competent municipal business authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the 2004 AML Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02: (1) each UBO, general partner, manager, and authorized signatory must be screened against the Luxembourg/EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council designation matrices, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, and EU terrorist lists; (2) Politically Exposed Persons status, including family members and close associates, must be assessed for all non-Luxembourg Asian stakeholders under Article 4 of the 2004 AML Law, and any PEP hit triggers enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; (3) corporate-level screening against corruption watchlists and adverse media databases; (4) re-screening at 90-day intervals and immediately upon any ownership, management, or name variation; (5) mandatory transaction refusal and escalation protocol where a screening match confirms a sanctions designation or unexplained PEP-related risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), electronic filing platform at www.lbr.lu integrated with the guichet.lu one-stop-shop
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All RCS filings and corporate names must be rendered in Latin-script French, German, or Luxembourgish; the mandatory suffix 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or 'SCSp' must appear in the legal name. Asian brand, heritage, or descriptive terms must be transliterated into romanized French-readable form; logographic characters (Hanzi, Kanji, Thai script) are inadmissible in the registered name. The proposed name must be phonetically and graphically distinguishable from all prior registered entities, protected trade names, and relevant trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Banque' / 'Bank' / 'Credit' (reserved for licensed credit institutions under CSSF supervision)
'Assurance' / 'Insurance' / 'Reassurance' (reserved for licensed insurance and reinsurance undertakings)
'Fiducie' / 'Fiduciary' / 'Trust' (reserved for regulated trust and corporate service providers)
'Europe' / 'International' / 'Worldwide' (permitted only where demonstrably accurate for actual commercial scope)
'Societe Anonyme' / 'SA' / 'SARL' (incompatible corporate-form suffixes that misrepresent SCSp liability)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR performs name availability and differentiation checks ex officio at filing; no discrete pre-registration name reservation instrument exists in Luxembourg. Upon formal rejection, the applicant may re-file with a revised name within the pending application dossier or submit a reasoned written representation to the RCS within 15 days. An adverse final decision may be appealed before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) by principal action, with interim relief available via the refere procedure. Practical continuation is achieved by filing a modified name rather than pursuing an extension.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted for the SCSp registered seat (siege) only where a physical Luxembourg address, local mail-handling capacity, and administrative control are maintained; however, for the ISIC 4721 physical grocery retail licence, the entity must hold actual storefront, inventory storage, and hygiene-compliant commercial premises in Luxembourg. A virtual-office-only arrangement cannot satisfy the statutory conditions for the autorisation d'etablissement or the ALVA food-safety establishment registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderately high - quantified at 60% annual probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection - driven by municipal commercial licensing controls, food hygiene audits by ALVA under EU Regulation 852/2004 for specialty imported-food retail, cash-handling compliance surveillance at checkout lines, and the Luxembourg tax administration's substance-verification reviews of registered offices.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); Law of 12 July 2013 creating the Société en Commandite Spéciale; Law of 19 December 2012 on the RCS and Luxembourg Business Registers; applicable provisions on special limited partnerships and RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS); publication through the Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and the corresponding RCS filing form, filed by the general partner through the LBR electronic filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, no paid-up capital, and no bank escrow or capital certificate requirement for an SCSp. Contributions are freely agreed in the partnership agreement and may be made in cash, in kind, or as an obligation to contribute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING OF THE GENERAL PARTNER. 1. RESOLVED that the SCSp's partnership agreement presented to this meeting is approved, adopted and subscribed by the participants. 2. RESOLVED that the registered office of the SCSp is established at the Luxembourg registered office appearing in the deed and the Luxembourg Business Registers is designated as the registration authority. 3. RESOLVED that [General Partner], acting as sole general partner, is authorized, under sole signature, to execute and file all incorporation forms, appoint the first manager, receive the partners' capital contributions, and apply for registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés. 4. RESOLVED that all prior actions taken in connection herewith are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of general partner and adoption of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and partners meeting; optionally a Luxembourg notary where real property contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold authorization meetings of any corporate partner and execute the SCSp partnership agreement. Ensure the agreement identifies the general partner, the object, the registered office, the contribution commitments and the profit-sharing rules. A notarial deed is not required for an SCSp unless Luxembourg real estate is contributed or specific legal formalities require authentication.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and passport copies of all partners
KYC/AML documentation of beneficial owners
Corporate authorizations and board resolutions where a corporate general partner is appointed
Copy of the registered-office provider's acceptance or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is queried, pass a corrective resolution and re-execute or amend the deed; for notarial deeds, request the notary's rectification before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name screen and registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: LBR RCS online name search and registered-office provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability of the proposed SCSp name against the RCS and trademark registers. Confirm the precise Luxembourg registered office and obtain a written acceptance from the landlord or registered-office provider. If desired, reserve the name via the LBR online reservation service.
required_dossiers: Name availability search result
Written registered-office acceptance or lease documentation
Landlord's identity and consent if required by the provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registration, select a distinctive alternate name or obtain a consent letter from the prior right-holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS creation filing and registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Registration Department and electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal RCS registration application using the SCSp structure code, upload the executed partnership agreement and supporting documents, and pay the LBR filing tariff. Include the identity of the general partner and managers, the designated registered office, the company object, and the declaration that managers are not disqualified.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement or constitutive deed
Completed RCS company creation form
Identity documents and address proof of all partners and managers
Declaration of non-bankruptcy/proper good conduct for each manager
Proof of payment of the LBR fee
If corporate general partner: commercial register extract and appointment resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS deficiency notice by resubmitting corrected forms and documents; if the application is refused, apply to the Luxembourg commercial court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS approval, the LBR publishes the registration notice in the RES. Verify the published notice for exact legal name, RCS number, registered office and manager details. Obtain the official RCS extract or business-register excerpt for transaction and licensing use.
required_dossiers: RCS registration notice wording
Official RCS extract or registration excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES publication contains an error, file a rectification request with the LBR and arrange for the corrected notice to be published in the RES.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social and operational identification follow-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); relevant sectoral authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS registration number, apply to the AEDT for VAT and direct tax identification where applicable and file the declaration of business activity. Register with the CCSS as an employer if staff will be engaged before opening. For food retailing, coordinate with the Luxembourg food-sector authorities for the separate operating approval.
required_dossiers: Official RCS extract
SCSp partnership agreement excerpt
Identification data of managers and partners
VAT/tax registration questionnaire
CCSS employer registration form and staff list if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-submit any rejected tax or social-security forms with the RCS extract; if a data mismatch blocks registration, seek correction of the RCS entry first.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate General for Business Establishment and SMEs; municipal commercial licensing service of the commune where the store operates.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for commercial retail under the Law of 30 May 2005 on business establishment, together with municipal commercial exploitation approval and any food business approval issued by the Luxembourg food/veterinary authorities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA: grocery retail falls below Annex II commercial development thresholds, provided gross floor area remains below the applicable 10,000 m² threshold. A simplified environmental registration or written environmental notice may still be required for refrigeration installations containing fluorinated greenhouse gases and for waste storage areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must be discharged to the municipal sewer only in compliance with communal discharge limits for pH, BOD5/COD, suspended solids, hydrocarbons and fats, and must pass through an approved grease/oil interceptor. Refrigeration and HVAC systems must comply with Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, including leak checks, leakage detection and recovery obligations. All waste, including food waste, packaging, fluorescent tubes and refrigerant oils, must be deposited only with authorized waste collectors and traceable under Luxembourg waste-tracking rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and rescue clearance from the communal fire inspection service and Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) covering the evacuation plan, fire alarm system and extinguishing equipment; structural inspection certificate for live loading, shelving and floor capacities; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and communal health approval for food retail premises before staff employment and public opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and myGuichet.lu as unified e-portals (www.aed.public.lu, www.impotsdirects.public.lu, www.lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Execute the SCSp partnership deed before a Luxembourg notary and file it with the Luxembourg Business Registers to obtain the RCS registration number and national matricule (business identification number issued via CTIE); (2) file VAT registration with the AED using the matricule — registration is compulsory upon commencement of any taxable economic activity where annual turnover exceeds the €35,000 small-business exemption threshold, and compulsory without threshold for non-resident traders; (3) receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 numeric digits); (4) register employer obligations with the ACD (payroll withholding) and the CCSS for social security where staff are employed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for income tax (partners are taxed directly on their allocable share); for VAT purposes the SCSp remains an independent taxable person in respect of its grocery-retail activity; territorial scope is worldwide taxation for Luxembourg-resident partners and Luxembourg-source taxation for non-resident partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box-style opacity election under the 15 December 2015 partnership tax law (effective 2017; Art. 4(2) LIR) permitting entity-level treatment where all partners are themselves subject to tax and where international classification symmetry so requires; ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules apply where tax classification differs across partner jurisdictions; no opacity election is available in respect of VAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Luxembourg VAT Code (LTV) transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC — no separate GST regime; in-store retail supplies of imported Asian foodstuffs qualify for the EU Annex III reduced rate of 8% while listed essential commodities attract the 3% super-reduced rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual turnover (exclusive of VAT) triggering the small-business exemption under Art. 28 LTV; registration is mandatory above this ceiling and is required regardless of turnover for any non-established trader engaged in taxable retail sales in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing in Factur-X 3.0 format through the Peppol network with phased public-sector deadlines through 2026; no mandatory real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC), fiscal clearance or digital stamping applies to grocery retail; periodic VAT returns are filed electronically via the e-TVA/myGuichet portal on monthly, quarterly or annual cycles, with SAF-T audit files available on ACD demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to physical exports of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU within 90 days of transfer of ownership, provided the exporter retains complete transport and commercial evidence; zero-rating for intra-EU dispatches to registered business customers requires a valid EU VAT ID of the recipient with reverse charge in the destination state; related cross-border retail services to non-EU recipients may be zero-rated where use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU; the SCSp as a registered VAT person recovers related input VAT through its periodic returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — electronically lodged full/summary SAD accepted by Luxembourg Customs (DUAS/PLDA system) evidencing physical departure of goods from the EU
Bill of Lading — or Air Waybill/CMR transport document showing dispatch to a non-EU destination within the 90-day statutory export window
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank and exchange-control evidence confirming receipt of export sales proceeds from the foreign counterparty, retained for audit substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AED and Luxembourg Customs jointly audit export files (customs declarations, transport logs, bank/FX payment traces); unjustified zero-rating is clawed back at the applicable rate (8% for grocery items or 17% standard) plus 0.9% monthly late-payment interest and an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the evaded VAT in negligence cases; deliberate falsification of export documents attracts criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to five years, with a 5-year statutory reassessment window extended where fraud or forged documentation is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), as the national Central Bank and National Competent Authority reporting into the Eurosystem/European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institution licensing, AML/CFT compliance, and market conduct for banks and payment/e-money institutions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of current-account and capital-account items applies pursuant to Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EU free movement of capital framework; Luxembourg imposes no exchange control licensing, no convertibility restrictions and no segregation of retained earnings or blocked-account rules for either the SCSp or its foreign partners. Profit remittance and capital repatriation are unrestricted for Eurozone, EEA and third-country counterparties that are not subject to EU/UN targeted financial sanctions. The only practical frictions are (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declaration by the beneficiary/paying bank for cross-border payments of at least EUR 12,500, (ii) EU/UN/HMT sanction screening of counterparties, and (iii) CSSF anti-money-laundering source-of-funds due diligence on capital subscriptions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion obligation exists in Luxembourg or at EU level. Exporters and retail importers are not required to repatriate foreign sales proceeds within any timeline, and no mandatory percentage of export receipts must be exchanged into Euro. Proceeds may be retained indefinitely in EUR or freely convertible foreign currency accounts held at Luxembourg or other EEA-licensed credit institutions, subject solely to the banks' BoP reporting threshold of EUR 12,500 per wire and standard invoice/transport documentary retention for anti-money-laundering and tax audits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency current account) and ancillary Capital Subscription sub-account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (sub-account for committed limited-partner capital)
Operational Account with dedicated trade-services module
Capital Escrow / Partnership capital custody account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, ancillary use only. A Luxembourg- or other EEA-authorised EMI passporting under PSD2 can provide multi-currency IBANs, API-driven treasury screens, card acquiring for the grocery-retail entity (POS/Interac) and expedited FX for incidental balances. However, an EMI is not licensed for credit/escrow, cannot issue commercial import letters of credit, often caps account balances below institutional capital-injection levels, and may decline a Luxembourg-domiciled, non-resident-owned SCSp because of opaque-partnership KYC friction. Consequently the EMI shall be limited to a float/acquiring overlay while BCL-licensed Tier-1 banks carry the principal liquidity and LC rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The general partner's authorised signatories are statutorily required to complete an in-person (or equivalent secure videoconference, accepted at bank discretion) KYC interview with the bank's Luxembourg compliance officer before account activation; a single legal representative may appear in person while remote approved-person attestations are obtained for non-resident limited partners. Physical presence of every limited partner is not mandatory; notarised/apostilled constituent documents (partnership agreement, powers of attorney) and a professional-legaliser certificate are sufficient for each non-resident UBO, provided no PEP/sanctions flags are triggered. Fully automated non-face-to-face onboarding of an SCSp is rare and escalates to the MLRO; remote opening is routinely refused for high-risk source jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of SCSp ownership: non-resident limited partners with a nominee general partner and no Luxembourg legal personality.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS certified extract; notarised limited partnership agreement; CSSF-aligned UBO declaration and register filing; LEI certificate; tax-residence certificates of each partner; group structure chart; sworn source-of-wealth statements for each capital subscriber.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance mismatch: Luxembourg-domiciled partnership centrally managed overseas and lacking physical footprint for retail activity in Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance playbook: Luxembourg management-services agreement; office lease or co-working agreement; payroll/hiring contracts for at least two local officers; Luxembourg board minutes and document-flow evidence; commercial licence and health import permits; profit-and-liquidity forecasts for the first 24 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds plausibility for cross-border capital injections from Asian shareholders/affiliates into a grocery-retail entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call schedule; injection wire plan with BoP purpose code S301; audited parent/affiliate balance sheets; bank reference letters; notarised equity-subscription deeds; gift/inheritance documentation if personal capital; granular store-asset purchase agreements; anti-fraud confirmation of beneficial receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-supplier concentration in higher-risk cleared corridors (China, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan) combined with cash-heavy retail POS cashflow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Acquirer and POS (Interac) terminal contracts; historical merchant sales register; approved supplier list with KYC; signed import purchase contracts and pro-forma invoices; freight-forwarder agreements and bills of lading; Luxembourg veterinary/health certificates and consumer-affairs authorization; Denied-Party-screening report for all counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: each limited-partner capital subscription is remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer if within EEA) from the partner's bank to the SCSp's capital-subscription account; wire field 70 (remittance) cites the SCSp LEI, the partnership-agreement article authorising the drawdown, and the capital-account ratio; the Luxembourg beneficiary bank assigns the ECB/EUBoP purpose code 'S301 – injection of capital into an investment vehicle/enterprise' and files the BCL statistical return for any transfer with value ≥ EUR 12,500; verification is completed through a pre-provisioned source-of-funds and UBO file so the bank can release the credit without AML escalation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant and SWIFT MT103 for value-date supplier settlement; for large or repeated Asian commodities procurement the bank issues irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (MT700 issue, MT707 amendment) with sight or usance drafts payable at the beneficiary's confirming bank in the supplier's country; TARGET2 is used for EUR legs requiring real-time gross settlement; all payments are screened against EU/UN sanctions and requester-BoP reporting is automatically filed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNH deliverable outright forwards and swaps
EUR/JPY deliverable outright forwards and FX swaps
EUR/USD spot, outright forwards and FX swaps (USD-denominated commodity procurement)
EUR/CNH cross-currency interest-rate swaps (ISDA 2002, with EMIR clearing/CSA collateral if bank counterparty is a financial counterparty)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS registration maintenance fee and register-continuation payment (taxe annuelle RCS / LBR annual fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually per LBR invoicing cycle; invoice generally issued in the first calendar quarter and payable within one month of issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest, enforced collection by LBR, and after formal notice and unresolved default, administrative strike-off and deregistration from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial-owner confirmation and transfer-update declaration (déclaration annuelle de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within one month after the annual anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any transfer of partnership interests must be filed within one month of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250 for late or inaccurate filings, criminal fines for wilful non-compliance; persistent failure may trigger RBE enforcement and denial of RBE clearance certificates, but does not by itself cause RCS strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold applies to the SCSp itself because it lacks separate legal personality and is not subject to Luxembourg annual accounts publication or audit requirements; where the general partner is a Luxembourg S.A. or S.à r.l., that managing entity remains subject to ordinary audit thresholds (total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 9.1 million, average headcount 50; any two of three trigger audit).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as transposed from EU Accounting Directive; IFRS may be adopted voluntarily. The SCSp is not required to file annual accounts with the RCS, but business records and financial statements, if voluntarily prepared, must follow proper accounting principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must confirm the RBE data at least once every calendar year, ordinarily within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; each transfer of a partnership interest or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within one month after the change, and the annual confirmation cannot be used as a substitute for the transfer-update filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and representative powers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – USD 4,000 per year (Luxembourg registered office and administrative agent; may include general-partner administration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (statutorily exempt); USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 if an investor-mandated independent audit or review is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City rate, comprising 15% corporate income tax (IRC), 1.05% unemployment solidarity surcharge (contribution au fonds pour l'emploi), and 6.75% municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal); the exact effective burden deviates by commune because the municipal multiplier ranges from 200% to 300%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday applies to physical grocery retail under ISIC 4721. Available general reliefs: 17-year net operating loss carryforward, 80% exempt integrated IP box regime (not relevant to supermarket operations), and the optional Luxembourg investment tax credit for qualifying tangible assets. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, so the 24.94% headline charge is borne at the individual partner level; if the entity validly elects Article 165bis LIR corporate taxation, the SCSp itself becomes subject to CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (annual Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax declaration) combined with the SCSp partner allocation annex, submitted electronically to the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) through the secure E-Déclaration / MyGuichet.lu professional portal; net wealth tax components, if any, use separate Form 100-series filings only when the Article 165bis LIR election applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the commercial book-year of the SCSp; the default is the calendar year for the Asian supermarket grocery hub closing its books on 31 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: A Luxembourg fiscal year ending 31 December N must be declared by 31 May N+1 in strict law. Where the return is filed electronically and the ACD has not served an assessment notice, commercial practice generally tolerates submission up to 31 December N+1; professional advisers should not rely on this without written ACD confirmation because late-filing surcharges start to run after the statutory date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCSL registration number, Luxembourg tax matricule, entity legal form as SCSp, registered office address, and the fiscal year commencement and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate partners, provide full legal name, country of residence, home tax identification number, and percentage of partnership profit rights; the ACD requires that the non-resident partner declare its representative in Luxembourg and evidence a substantive Luxembourg permanent establishment (the physical grocery store) if claiming allocable business expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial balance sheet with inventory value, stock purchases of Asian condiments and vegetables, trade receivables, POS cash positions, payables to related-party suppliers, and the capital accounts of each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident beneficial partner must reconcile its capital contribution and withdrawal history with the SCSp books; unexplained negative capital accounts from distributions in excess of profit share are treated as a loan or a dividend-equivalent under Luxembourg tax recharacterization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from grocery sales, including all cash and card receipts recorded through the POS system, adjusted for intra-group intercompany sales if the SCSp acts as a hub importer for affiliated supermarkets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure that a POS sales summary and daily Z-reports are retained at the Luxembourg store; electronic sales suppression or destruction of cash register data is treated as deliberate fraud and will extinguish any Treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of imported goods sold, warehouse rental, staff wages, social contributions, store utilities, logistics, credit-card processing fees, depreciation on cooling units and shelving, and properly evidenced business travel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses invoiced by a related Asian supplying entity must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; Luxembourg's arm's-length principle permits a standard retail resale margin but disallows unrelated marketing or management fees charged against the store's grocery margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit converted to taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses such as fines, 50% of undocumented hospitality, and any Luxembourg net wealth tax paid where the Article 165bis election is effective.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner's share is computed on the same taxable base as an identical Luxembourg-resident partner; no ring-fencing of the retail loss against a foreign partner's other Luxembourg income is permitted once the permanent establishment is conceded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Previously assessed tax losses deducted against current-year taxable income under the 17-year carryforward rule; no carryback is available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses pass through the SCSp to the partners. A non-resident partner may apply its allocated Luxembourg loss in its home jurisdiction only if the applicable double tax treaty allocates Luxembourg loss absorption; the ACD nevertheless reports the cumulative loss history on Form 600 for potential future set-off in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of the investment tax credit, the IP box exemption if any certified intangible income exists, and withholding-tax credits on any portfolio dividends received by or through the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may not directly claim Luxembourg investment tax credits unless the credit is generated by the Luxembourg permanent establishment; the managing partner should separately attach a credit-flow schedule for tax transparency purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 50 - Tax computation and partner allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final assessed corporate income tax and municipal business tax where elected, or, in transparent mode, the proportional allocation of taxable income to each SCSp partner with a Luxembourg disclosure annex.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the SCSp is transparent, the ACD sends no separate CIT assessment to the SCSp; each non-resident corporate partner receives a partnership income statement for use in the home filing and in substantiating any external branch exemption claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax under Article 168 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per commenced month on unpaid corporate income and municipal business tax. A taxpayer that knowingly files an incomplete profit schedule of the SCSp faces a criminal fraud fine of up to double the tax evaded and, for directing partners, imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Luxembourg imposes a statutory 15% dividend withholding tax on distributions of profits by a Luxembourg tax-resident corporate entity. An SCSp is fiscally transparent and generally has no legal personality, so profit allocations to partners are not treated as dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the SCSp level. If, however, the SCSp sits above a Luxembourg operating SARL that distributes grocery-hub profits, that upstream dividend is subject to the full 15% WHT unless the parent-subsidiary participation exemption or a treaty-reduced rate is granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced or zero dividend WHT under a Luxembourg double tax treaty, the recipient partner must (i) prove beneficial ownership of the underlying Luxembourg dividend; (ii) obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority covering the exact dividend payment date; (iii) submit the TRC and a WHT relief/refund questionnaire to the Luxembourg ACD through the MyGuichet e-filing channel, together with evidence of the SCSp's commercial substance such as the store lease, payroll data, and bank account statements; and (iv) respond to any ACD substance questionnaire if the partner is in a jurisdiction with zero or low corporate tax. Processing of refund claims normally takes 6 to 12 months; the ACD applies the look-through principle, so an SCSp itself will not obtain treaty relief unless the partner's certificate and the underlying economic substance are validated.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not levy withholding tax on ordinary arm's-length interest or royalty payments made by a Luxembourg taxpayer to non-residents, the statutory rate being 0%. This neutrality is preserved under most DTA protocols and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive. The 15% dividend WHT can nevertheless be reactivated by recharacterization where a purported interest or royalty stream is subordinated, profit-linked, or disguised as a distribution to a shell shareholder; payments to beneficiaries resident in an EU blacklisted jurisdiction may be subjected to a domestic anti-abuse withholding measure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Luxembourg constituent entity must prepare and file the Master File and Local File where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeded EUR 750 million in the preceding fiscal year, and must file Country-by-Country Reporting through the Luxembourg ACD for the same EUR 750 million threshold. For the Asian supermarket grocery hub operating below this threshold, no automatic TP file is due, but Article 56 LIR and the ACD Transfer Pricing Circular (Circular LIR 56/1 of 28 January 2016) require that all intra-group purchasing, centralized procurement services, and management-fee arrangements with affiliated Asian suppliers be contemporaneously documented, benchmarked, and disclosed to the tax auditor upon request within a reasonable period.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code or a separate ESR filing regime for SCSp vehicles. Instead, substance requirements are embedded in the GAAR under Article 6 AO, the tax abuse doctrine in Article 56 LIR, and the ACD Circular LIR 102/2 applicable to holding and partnership structures. A supermarket SCSp inherently satisfies substance when it employs store staff under Luxembourg contracts, leases or owns a commercial premise, keeps physical inventory of imported Asian condiments and vegetables, holds POS and banking records in Luxembourg, and takes management decisions locally. Absent such operations, the ACD may disregard the SCSp as an abusive intermediary, deny treaty benefits, and allocate the grocery margin directly to the foreign partner's head office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Deliberate Tax Under-Declaration and Cash Sales Suppression
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp grocery hub records only card transactions while omitting cash sales at the Asian supermarket POS, suppresses Z-reports, maintains off-book inventory purchases, or pays employees undeclared cash wages derived from grocery revenue, thereby reducing Luxembourg taxable income below the true commercial result.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD reassesses income at the aggregate 24.94% Luxembourg City rate, applies a late-filing or concealed-income surcharge of up to 10%, charges monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and assesses criminal tax fraud penalties. In a criminal prosecution for deliberate concealment, the court may impose a fine of up to double the evaded tax and imprisonment of the directing partner for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or managing partner who signs a false Form 600 or directs cash suppression is personally exposed to criminal liability and civil restitution for the evaded corporate income tax and municipal business tax. Piercing of the corporate veil is available against the SCSp's general partner when the SCSp is a transparent conduit and the true beneficiary controls the retail operation; courts may additionally impose a travel ban and disqualify the manager from holding Luxembourg directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Substance Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the SCSp as an Asian supermarket grocery hub without any actual store, stock, staff, or local management, then using the SCSp's pass-through status to channel retail margins or to obtain treaty WHT relief on dividends from a Luxembourg operating company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD can disregard the SCSp under Article 6 AO and Article 56 LIR, reattribute all Luxembourg-source income to the true foreign enterprise, deny the treaty reduced rates, impose the full 15% withholding tax on actual or recharacterized distributions, and issue penalty assessments plus monthly default interest. The Luxembourg court may impose administrative fines and, for cross-border conduit arrangements, refer the case to the tax criminal chamber.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal director of a shell SCSp faces joint and several liability for the corporate income tax, interest, and penalties when it is shown that the director was a mere accommodation party. Civil restitution can extend to the value of assets diverted out of Luxembourg, and the director can be barred from operating a Luxembourg-registered business for a fixed term.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Mispricing of Asian Grocery Imports
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing exported Asian condiments, sauces, rice, and vegetables from a related-party supplier in Singapore, Hong Kong, or a no/low-tax jurisdiction at inflated or manipulated transfer prices, or alternatively buying below cost from a related party to stabilize a permanent loss position, in order to shift supermarket profit out of Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD makes a primary transfer-pricing adjustment restoring the grocery hub profit to the arm's-length resale price margin, adds a secondary adjustment treating the excess paid as a deemed distribution subject to 15% withholding tax, and levies interest at 0.6% per month. Failure to produce the contemporaneous Local File documentation entitles the tax auditor to presume income and to impose a documentation-related penalty alongside the tax adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The JV director or procurement officer who knowingly signs inflated supplier agreements can be held personally liable for the levied withholding tax and penalty where Luxembourg courts find bad faith participation. In aggravated schemes involving invoices for goods never delivered, the directors face criminal liability for forgery and tax fraud, with cumulative custodial sentences.
